title: Assessment of the Impact of Informal Seed System on Production of the Malt Barley in Potential Areas of Amhara Region in Ethiopia
content: To asses Impact of the informal seed system on the production of the malt barley in Ethiopia. The study purposefully selected seed samples from each of the two zones, Awi and South Gondar, using 60 sample homes and farmers. From every sample, 1000 g of malted barley seeds were taken for investigation of seed quality. The results indicate that Farmers mostly choose their seeds based on seed size (15. 23%), marketability (21.42%), and color (48.47%). The study revealed that the most common source of seeds was their saved stock. In the south Gondar zone, 2.7% of smallholder farmers sourced seeds from the integrated seed system, 9.3% from the formal seed system, and 88% through the informal seed system. For Traveller, Ibon, Holker, and Fatima, the seed moisture content was within and below the Ethiopian seed standard of 11.35, 17.35, 14.0, and 12.1, respectively. These imply that standard germination varied significantly between the seed samples. Moreover, the national seed specifications were met by the average germination percentage. There were notable differences in each sample's germination rate, shoot and root lengths, seedling dry weight, and vigor index 1. formal seed systems should be crucial for improving the malted barley seed system.
